T: Love, honour and a very complicated wedding.
D: A Brooklyn mob hitman falls for a woman who turns out to be in the same line of work.
P: Serve dessert at the wedding, when Charley first spots Irene.
S: olives, salami and marinated mushrooms for the reception
Marinate button mushrooms (blanched 1 minute) in oil, lemon, garlic and parsley overnight. Platter with salami, olives and marinated artichokes.
Chilled saffron risotto rolled around a cube of mozzarella, floured, egged and crumbed, fried at 175C until deep gold. Marinara for dipping.
Zucchini batons tossed in flour then dipped in a light batter of flour and sparkling water, fried at 185C, salt and lemon.
M: Ziti in slow sausage sugo layered with seasoned ricotta and mozzarella, baked at 200C until blistered.
Veal escalopes pounded thin, floured and seared 60 seconds a side, pan sauce of white wine, lemon, capers and stock, cold butter whisked in.
W: Amaretti: whisk 2 egg whites stiff, fold in 250g almond meal, 200g sugar and almond extract. Roll in icing sugar, bake at 170C for 15 minutes until crackled.
K: the toast at the Prizzi wedding where Charley first spots Irene

Fresh white peach purée topped slowly with cold prosecco in flutes, with a squeeze of lemon to keep it bright. Peel and stone 2 ripe white peaches. Blend with 2 tsp lemon juice and 1 tsp caster sugar until smooth, then chill for 30 minutes. Spoon 40ml purée into each of 4 chilled flutes. Top slowly with 120ml prosecco each, pouring down the side of the glass. Stir once with a long spoon and serve straight away.

dishes.make_ahead: Mushrooms need to marinate overnight, serve at room temperature

steps.text: Blanch the mushrooms in boiling water for 1 minute and drain well.
Toss with olive oil, lemon juice, garlic and parsley. Refrigerate covered overnight.
Serve on a platter with the salami, olives and artichokes.
Cut the zucchini into batons, pat dry and toss with 30g of the flour.
Whisk the remaining flour with the sparkling water into a light batter.
Heat the oil to 185C and fry the battered batons in small batches for 3 minutes until crisp and golden.
Drain, season with salt and serve with lemon.

dishes.make_ahead: Assemble up to 1 day ahead, keep chilled; add 10 minutes to the bake

steps.text: Remove the sausages from their casings and brown in the oil, breaking up the meat.
Add the onion for 5 minutes, then the garlic for 1 minute.
Add the passata, water and oregano and simmer gently, stirring.
Boil the ziti for 2 minutes less than the packet time and drain. Mix the ricotta with the seasoning.
Layer pasta, sugo, ricotta and mozzarella in an ovenproof dish.
Bake at 200C for 25 minutes until blistered and rest for 10 minutes.
Whisk the egg whites to stiff peaks in a clean bowl.
Gently fold in the almond meal, caster sugar and almond extract.
Shape into 20 small balls, roll in icing sugar and space on lined trays.
Bake at 170C for 15 minutes until crackled and lightly golden.
Cool on the trays for 10 minutes, then move to a rack.

dishes.make_ahead: Purée up to 1 day ahead, keep chilled

steps.text: Peel and stone the peaches, blend with the lemon juice and sugar until smooth.
Chill the purée for 30 minutes.
Spoon some purée into each chilled flute and top slowly with prosecco poured down the side. Stir once and serve straight away.

dishes.make_ahead: Risotto up to 1 day ahead; fry just before serving

steps.text: Cook the rice in the stock with the saffron to a firm risotto, stir in the parmesan and cool completely.
Roll into balls around cubes of mozzarella.
Roll in flour, egg and breadcrumbs.
Fry at 180C in batches until gold.
Warm the marinara and serve alongside.

dishes.make_ahead: Up to 2 days chilled; keep the escarole fresh and add when reheating

ingredients.item: tiny pasta such as acini di pepe

steps.text: Mix the veal with the egg, breadcrumbs and parmesan and roll into tiny balls.
Simmer the stock with the carrot, add the meatballs and cook gently.
Add the pasta and escarole and cook until tender.
Season and serve hot.
Pound the veal thin, season and dust with flour.
Sear the veal fast in oil and a little butter, about 1 minute a side, and set aside.
Add the wine and lemon juice to the pan, reduce, then add the capers and swirl in the remaining butter.
Return the veal to warm through and scatter with parsley.

dishes.make_ahead: Up to 1 day ahead, keep frozen; scrape before serving

steps.text: Simmer the sugar, water and zest for 5 minutes, then cool.
Stir in the lemon juice and pour into a shallow tray.
Freeze, scraping with a fork every 30 minutes for 3 hours until light and fluffy.
Serve in small cups.
Count five sugared almonds into each bag and tie.
Brew four short espressos.
Serve with a small pour of anisette on the side.

edition.tagline: Love, honour and a very complicated wedding.
edition.cue: Serve dessert at the wedding, when Charley first spots Irene.

s.note: Lemon marinated mushrooms, salami, mixed olives and tender artichokes.
s.how: Blanch 200g button mushrooms in boiling water for 1 minute and drain well. Toss with 2 tbsp olive oil, juice of half a lemon, 1 crushed garlic clove and 1 tbsp chopped parsley. Refrigerate covered overnight. Serve on a platter with 100g salami, 120g mixed olives and 150g drained marinated artichokes for four people.

s.note: Crisp battered zucchini batons with salt and fresh lemon.
s.how: Cut 2 medium zucchini, about 400g, into batons and pat dry. Toss with 30g plain flour. Whisk 100g plain flour with 150ml cold sparkling water to a light batter. Heat neutral oil in a deep sturdy pan to 185°C. Dip the batons in batter and fry in small batches for 3 minutes until crisp and golden. Drain, season with 1/4 tsp salt and serve with the remaining half lemon cut into wedges.

m.note: Slow sausage sugo, seasoned ricotta and mozzarella, baked until blistered.
m.how: Remove 400g Italian sausages from their casings. Brown in 1 tbsp olive oil for 8 minutes, breaking up the meat. Add 1 diced onion and cook 5 minutes, then 2 crushed garlic cloves for 1 minute. Add 700g passata, 150ml water and 1 tsp dried oregano. Simmer gently for 45 minutes, stirring. Boil 350g ziti or penne for 2 minutes less than the packet time. Mix 250g ricotta with 1/4 tsp each salt and pepper. Layer the pasta and sausage sugo with spoonfuls of ricotta in an ovenproof dish, scattering 200g mozzarella between layers and over the top. Bake at 200°C conventional for 25 minutes until piping hot and blistered; rest 10 minutes before serving.

w.note: Crackled amaretti with almond meal, sugar and a snowy icing coat.
w.how: Heat the oven to 170°C conventional. Whisk 2 egg whites to stiff peaks in a clean bowl. Gently fold in 250g almond meal, 200g caster sugar and 1/2 tsp almond extract. Shape into 20 small balls, roll in 40g icing sugar and space on lined trays. Bake 15 minutes until crackled and lightly golden. Cool on the trays for 10 minutes, then transfer to a rack. Serve five small cookies each, or save extras in an airtight tin.

d.note: Fresh white peach purée topped slowly with cold prosecco in flutes, with a squeeze of lemon to keep it bright.
d.how: Peel and stone 2 ripe white peaches. Blend with 2 tsp lemon juice and 1 tsp caster sugar until smooth, then chill for 30 minutes. Spoon 40ml purée into each of 4 chilled flutes. Top slowly with 120ml prosecco each, pouring down the side of the glass. Stir once with a long spoon and serve straight away.
